newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends up 1.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends up 1.6 pct.

text.p: * Runup seen extending to Ayala and Benpres on Friday
The Manila share index climbed by 52.55 points, or 1.60 percent, to 3,328.38 points at Thursday's close propelled by heavy buying in blue chips led by Petron Corp.
"We saw a lot of people moving out of the speculatives to index-linked issues such as Petron and PLDT," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities.
Value turnover was heavy at 3.15 billion pesos.
"There may be some momentum tommorrow on Benpres and Ayala and we may head towards the 3,374 all time high," said Cilette Liboro, research head, at Citisecurities Inc.

The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) temporarily stopped at 9:45 a.m. (0145 GMT) on Thursday trading in shares of seven companies which participated in the bidding for privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS).

A consortium, in which Ayala Corp is a member, was considered as having posted the best bid for the east zone while another group, in which Benpres is a member, was considered the best bidder for the west zone.
The suspension on the shares was supposed to be lifted 30 minutes after brokers were informed of the best bidder.
But the market closed before the PSE could lift the suspension. The bourse's surveillance department said trading in the shares would resume on Friday.
Oil refiner Petron Corp was among the top 10 heavily traded shares and closed at 10.50 pesos, up 80 centavos or 8.25 percent from the previous close.
Buying in Petron was boosted by Wednesday's news that the Philippines had advanced its date for full deregulation of the oil industry by a month to Febuary 8.
Gainers swamped losers 83 to 53 with 62 unchanged issues.
